guard: an issued caller's journal and per-goal progress rows carry the plain triple, the subject the endpoint publishes progress on and the client submits journal work on
why: The generation rides the request and reply rails and nothing else. A grant row that carries it
on the epe goal-progress plane names a subject the endpoint never publishes, so an issued
caller's spawn is accepted, the seat joins, and the caller still reports no terminal within its
deadline; measured live as a 40s wait on every spawn through an instrument. The journal row has
the same shape and the same failure. Each mutation puts the generation back into one row.

mutations.name: the per-goal progress row is minted with the generation
mutations.expectRed: issued per-goal progress row is the plain triple

mutations.name: the journal row is minted with the generation
mutations.expectRed: issued journal row is the plain triple

mutations.name: instance-only emission also includes the default class one row
mutations.expectRed: request row: instance-only omits every class/scatter row
mutations.note: The view is useful only if every manager request is confined to the selected instance.

mutations.name: drop the mint-time bound on the composed user JWT
mutations.expectRed: six 4096-char allowSubscribe channels (each individually valid) are refused at the mint, naming the size and the bound
mutations.note: Every individual channel passes assertValidChannel and the composed JWT still exceeds the 65536-byte control line (six 4096-character channels minted a 71,569-byte JWT); only the byte check on the assembled JWT catches the composition, so removing it must red the six-channel cell first.
